findings.claim: The fold's close test (if (n !== 1) break) treats a run of two or more backslashes before a backtick inside a backtick span as closing. The measured transport treats a typed run as escaped whenever ceil(n/2) is odd: n = 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10 and so on. At n = 2, 5 and 6 the tokenizer closes the span at a backtick bash treats as literal. Every later backtick then pairs differently: the real closing backtick is read as an opener (or a single quote in the body opens an outer quote), and the statements after the substitution are swallowed into a span or a quote that the rows never read. This is read 4 F1's swallow with the direction flipped, and this fold introduced it. Main and 9b085e1d deny each of these commands. The msys-body-slash locator does not catch them, because its own escaped() also pairs closes by the n === 1 rule. The code comment, the test comment and the changeset parenthetical all state a rule the transport contradicts at n = 2. The halving rationale argues the other way: halving turns two into one, and one is escaped. The locator's fail-closed argument for openers does not carry over to closers, because a close read too early is not fail-closed.
findings.counterexample: Deciding probe: a three-way verdict run (main dist, 9b085e1d source transpiled, a0d6d39a dist) plus the argv probe under the Bash tool. Minimal shape: x=`echo 'q<2 backslashes>`'` ; gh pr comment 5 --body /x. main deny msys-body-slash, 9b085e1d deny msys-body-slash, a0d6d39a ALLOW. The same shape with a sed -i whose expression has a backslash: deny sed-i-escape on main and 9b085e1d, ALLOW on a0d6d39a. Under the Bash tool, the same shape with the node argv-echo script in place of gh printed the program's argument line: the program after the substitution runs. Longer form echo `echo 'q<n>`' r` ; <gh or sed> ; echo `echo z`: a0d6d39a allows at n = 2, 5 and 6 where main and 9b085e1d deny (measured RAN for n = 2 and n = 5). At n = 3, 4, 7 and 8 that form is a bash parse error, so the allow is harmless. Shape without quotes, echo `echo q<n>` r` ; sed -i ... ; echo `echo z`: sed-i-escape goes from deny to allow at every n of 2 or more (the program runs at n = 2, measured). Fix shape: one shared predicate for the tokenizer close and the locator close, escaped exactly when n mod 4 is 1 or 2; re-check that the fold's own n = 2 positive test stays denied; add the minimal shape as a positive test for both rows.

findings.claim: The fold says the uncapped msys-rev-path-subshell recursion is bounded by the text. It does terminate, but each nesting level adds a stack frame and re-tokenizes the inner text, so cost grows with depth times length. At a few thousand levels the row throws RangeError (Maximum call stack size exceeded), and transportShieldEvaluator has no catch around a row. The gate wrapper's stated posture is that any evaluation failure fails CLOSED. That is a verdict change beyond restoring the warning at six or more levels: a warn becomes a refusal, after one to two seconds. The fail-closed outcome was read from the wrapper's comment, not run end to end. The shape is adversarial only.
findings.counterexample: Deciding probe: N nested echo $( … ) around git show HEAD:a/b, timed on all three builds. Depth 2000 (16 KB): main warn in 1 ms, 9b085e1d allow in 3 ms, a0d6d39a warn in 163 ms. Depth 5000 (40 KB): main warn in 2 ms, 9b085e1d allow, a0d6d39a throws Maximum call stack size exceeded after 932 ms. Depth 10000: throws after 2304 ms. Fix shape: a generous cap (for example 256 levels) or an explicit work-list.

findings.claim: Outside this fold's diff, but the same mismatch on the opener side. It dates from 9b085e1d's span rule, not from a0d6d39a. Outside quotes the tokenizer consumes backslashes in pairs (the raw odd-run rule), so a typed run of two before a backtick is read as a literal backslash followed by an OPENER. Under the halving transport, bash sees one backslash, which escapes the backtick. The tokenizer then opens a span that swallows the statements up to the next backtick. The locator uses n === 1, so it reads the gh form correctly. The sed-i-escape and inline-body-escape rows inherit the tokenizer's reading. Raised so the F1 fix uses the same rule on both sides; the seat decides whether it is in scope.
findings.counterexample: Deciding probe: the three-way verdict run plus the argv probe. echo <2 backslashes>` ; sed -i with a backslash in its expression ; echo `z`: main deny sed-i-escape, 9b085e1d allow, a0d6d39a allow. Under the Bash tool, the same shape with node argv-echo in place of sed printed a literal backtick, then the program's argument line, then z: the program runs and is not in a substitution. The gh form of the same shape is denied on all three builds. At n = 1, 3 and 4 the tokenizer agrees with the transport.

verdict: read 5 on a0d6d39a (scoped to the backtick close test and the rev-path cap removal, 9b085e1d..a0d6d39a): as typed, 0 BLOCKING, 1 MATERIAL, 2 MINOR, 0 QUESTION; the leg did not name termination on F1. Its measurements: the transport's rule for a closing backtick behind a typed run of n backslashes, read one call per n under the Bash tool — n of 1 and 2 escaped, 3 and 4 close, 5 and 6 escaped (ceil(n/2) odd); a three-way replay over 21,680 real commands (1,090 with a backtick) found zero verdict changes across fold 7, with only 4 of them carrying a run of two or more before a backtick, so the replay is weak evidence on this rule and the constructed cases decide. Held at source: read 4's F1 fixed at three and four; the k > i bound harmless (a body of two or four backslashes denies as on main); a run of one, an escaped backtick inside the body before a real close, adjacent spans, an unterminated span after a run, $( ) inside a span and a span inside $( ), and a gh inside a span ending in a run of two or three unchanged; inside double quotes nothing changes (the tokenizer builds no span there); the cap removal restores the warning at six to nine levels and changes nothing else below about five thousand. Folded by the seat in the next commit: F1 MATERIAL (the fold-7 exactly-one close rule closed the span at n of 2, 5 and 6, where the transport escapes, re-pairing every later backtick and hiding the gh or sed after the span — deny on main and on the previous head, allow on a0d6d39a, the program measured running; an early close is not fail-closed, so the close is paired by the measured rule alone: n mod 4 of 1 or 2 escaped on the Bash tool on win32, threaded through ScanOptions from the payload and set by construction for the MSYS rows, bash's odd rule elsewhere; the locator's close uses the same rule), F2 (the uncapped recursion threw at about five thousand nested levels, which the wrapper reads as a refusal: capped at 256). Declined with the reason: F3 (the opener side consumes backslashes in pairs before reaching a backtick, so a typed run of two opens a span the transport would not; pre-existing from fold 6; rare; disclosed).
